items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I used to do all the Paul Weston dates and Paul wrote these beautiful string things.

ctx.x: Well said. What are you listening tastes? Well you said you turn on Art Tatum all the time at home.

I listen to Tatum, I listen to Oscar, I listen to Dick Hyman. Those are my three favorite pianists, as a pianist. I’ve got most of Peter Nero’s early stuff. He did what I always wanted to do and we couldn’t convince the people at CBS, I used to do all the Paul Weston dates and Paul wrote these beautiful string things. He was one of the better writers of that type of music. And we always wanted to do a piano thing with the string section and all that routine. And we couldn’t sell it to CBS and then RCA came out…
Music from fellows like John Coltrane that are seemingly very serious and filled with let’s say messages, did that ever appeal to you?
